headline: High-risk default data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because next-ai-draw-io uses broad network/MCP and external model APIs while Dagster can orchestrate data workflows, but direct pairwise coupling is undocumented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dagster has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, browser, or MCP surface, so direct injection into it is not documented. next-ai-draw-io can use MCP and natural-language commands, and if Dagster outputs are manually or file-shared into it, prompt-like content could steer downstream interpretation. The pathway is plausible but not default and the bridge is indirect.
conditions: IF Dagster outputs are copied into next-ai-draw-io prompts or MCP inputs
IF a shared file or workspace is introduced between the two agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste of raw Dagster logs into next-ai-draw-io
Add a human review step before any prompt ingestion
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to transferred artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dagster is local-only with no network egress, but next-ai-draw-io has broad network egress, external API calls, and handles API keys. If Dagster-managed files contain sensitive data and are opened in next-ai-draw-io, that content can be transmitted to third-party model backends by default. The pairwise leakage path is therefore dangerous even though shared storage is not explicitly documented.
conditions: IF Dagster-managed files contain secrets, PII, or regulated documents
IF next-ai-draw-io is configured to call a remote model provider
mitigations: Use only local/offline models in next-ai-draw-io
Redact sensitive fields before opening files
Separate sensitive Dagster outputs into a restricted folder
Rotate any API keys exposed to next-ai-draw-io
requires-engineering: enforce egress allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster cannot write files or modify git state, while next-ai-draw-io can process files and supports multiple instances. There is no direct write-write conflict shown, but if both are pointed at the same diagram or document workspace, concurrent edits can overwrite each other or create inconsistent artifacts. Uncertainty remains because shared mutable storage is not documented.
conditions: IF both agents are given the same writable workspace
IF next-ai-draw-io instances run concurrently on the same diagram files
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Lock shared files during edits
Avoid concurrent runs on the same artifact
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dagster can generate pipeline metadata or transformed outputs that next-ai-draw-io may render or summarize, and next-ai-draw-io uses natural-language commands plus AI-assisted visualization. If B treats A-produced content as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect diagrams or decisions. The interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF next-ai-draw-io consumes Dagster-generated text or metadata as source material
IF no human verification step is inserted before rendering or actioning
mitigations: Require source verification before rendering
Label Dagster outputs as untrusted inputs
Compare rendered diagrams against original pipeline specs
Use a review checklist for AI-generated summaries

E_compliance.rationale: Dagster itself shows no touched data classes or special residency constraints, while next-ai-draw-io explicitly handles PDFs, images, diagrams, and API keys and can send content to multiple external providers. If regulated documents are processed through B, retention and residency obligations can diverge from A's local-only posture. The mismatch is compliance-relevant even without a documented shared policy.
conditions: IF regulated documents or secrets are processed by next-ai-draw-io
IF the chosen model provider stores prompts outside the required jurisdiction
mitigations: Restrict B to non-regulated documents
Use a provider with a signed DPA and required residency
Disable retention where available
Document a data-handling policy for both tools
requires-engineering: implement jurisdiction-aware routing
